1: Mute sat Giray, with downcast eye, As though some spell in sorrow bound him, His slavish courtiers thronging nigh,
2: In sad expectance stood around him.
3: The lips of all had silence sealed,
4: Whilst, bent on him, each look observant,
5: Saw grief's deep trace and passion fervent
7: But the proud Khan his dark eye raising,
8: And on the courtiers fiercely gazing,
9: Gave signal to them to begone!
10: The chief, unwitnessed and alone, Now yields him to his bosom's smart,
12: Is traced the anguish of his heart;
13: As full fraught clouds on mirrors clear
15: What fills that haughty soul with pain? What thoughts such madd'ning tumults cause?
16: With Russia plots he war again?
17: Would he to Poland dictate laws? Say, is the sword of vengeance glancing?
19: Does bold revolt claim nature's right?
21: Or sabres of fierce foes advancing?
22: Ah no! no more his proud steed prancing Beneath him guides the Khan to war,--
23: Such thoughts his mind has banished far.
24: Has treason scaled the harem's wall, Whose height might treason's self appal,
25: And slavery's daughter fled his power,
26: To yield her to the daring Giaour? No! pining in his harem sadly, No wife of his would act so madly;
27: To wish or think they scarcely dare;
29: By wretches, cold and heartless, guarded,
30: Hope from each breast so long discarded;
32: Their beauties unto none revealed, They bloom within the harem's towers,
34: As in a hot-house bloom the flowers
35: Which erst perfumed Arabia's field. To them the days in sameness dreary,
37: And months and years pass slow away,
38: In solitude, of life grown weary,
39: Well pleased they see their charms decay.
40: Each day, alas! the past resembling,
41: Time loiters through their halls and bowers;
42: In idleness, and fear, and trembling,
43: The captives pass their joyless hours.
45: Their hearts in striving to deceive Into oblivion of distress,
48: Or by the noise of living streams,
49: In soft translucency meand'ring, To lose their thoughts in fancy's dreams,
52: But the vile eunuch too is there, In his base duty ever zealous,
53: Escape is hopeless to the fair
54: From ear so keen and eye so jealous.
56: He ruled the harem, order reigned Eternal there; the trusted treasure He watched with loyalty unfeigned,
58: His only law his chieftain's pleasure,
59: Which as the Koran he maintained.
61: His soul love's gentle flame derides,
62: And like a statue he abides
64: Nor prayers relax his temper rigid,
65: Nor timid sighs from tender breasts, To all alike the wretch is frigid.
67: He knows how woman's sighs can melt,
68: Freeman and bondman he had felt
69: Her art in days when he was younger;
70: Her silent tear, her suppliant look,
71: Which once his heart confiding shook,
72: Now move not,--he believes no longer!
73: When, to relieve the noontide heat, The captives go their limbs to lave,
76: Yield all their beauties to the wave,
77: No stranger eye their charms may greet, But their strict guard is ever nigh,
80: He constant, even in gloom of night,
81: Through the still harem cautious stealing,
84: From couch to couch his pathway feeling,
87: And whilst in sleep unguarded lying,
91: Should some loved name in dreams be sighed,

95: Whilst or to move or breathe scarce daring, The eunuch watches every look;

106: And o'er the marble cleave their way,
107: Whose golden scales are brightly glancing,

110: Serve sherbet to the beauteous fair,

120: Blest he who sees pale Death await him On Danube's ever glorious shore;
122: The girls of Paradise shall greet him, And sorrows ne'er afflict him more.
125: But he more blest, O beauteous Zarem!
126: Who quits the world and all its woes,
127: To clasp thy charms within the harem,
128: Thou lovelier than the unplucked rose!
129: They sing, but-where, alas! is Zarem,
130: Love's star, the glory of the harem?
131: Pallid and sad no praise she hears,
132: Deaf to all sounds of joy her ears,
133: Downcast with grief, her youthful form Yields like the palm tree to the storm,
135: Fair Zarem's dreams of bliss are o'er,
136: Her loved Giray loves her no more!
137: He leaves thee! yet whose charms divine Can equal, fair Grusinian! thine?
138: Shading thy brow, thy raven hair
139: Its lily fairness makes more fair;
140: Thine eyes of love appear more bright
141: Than noonday's beam, more dark than night;
142: Whose voice like thine can breathe of blisses,
143: Filling the heart with soft desire?
144: Like thine, ah! whose inflaming kisses
146: Who that has felt thy twining arms
147: Could quit them for another's charms?
148: Yet cold, and passionless, and cruel,
149: Giray can thy vast love despise,
150: Passing the lonesome night in sighs Heaved for another; fiercer fuel Burns in his heart since the fair Pole
153: Is placed within the chief's control.
156: Had borne in conquest from afar; Not long her love-enkindling eyes
157: Had gazed upon these foreign skies; Her aged father's boast and pride, She bloomed in beauty by his side;
159: Each wish was granted ere expressed.
161: She to his heart the object dearest,
162: His sole desire to see her blessed;
163: As when the skies from clouds are clearest,
164: Still from her youthful heart to chase
166: Hoping in after life that never Her woman's duties might efface
168: But oft that fancy would retrace
169: Life's blissful spring-time decked in flowers.
170: Her form a thousand charms unfolded, Her face by beauty's self was moulded,
172: Her dark blue eyes were full of fire,--
173: All nature's stores on her were lavished;
175: The magic harp with soft desire,
176: When touched by her, the senses ravished.
177: Warriors and knights had sought in vain
179: Maria's virgin heart to move, And many a youth in secret pain Pined for her in despairing love.
181: But love she knew not, in her breast
182: Tranquil it had not yet intruded,
183: Her days in mirth, her nights in rest,
185: Passed heedless, peace her bosom's guest. That time is past! The Tartar's force
186: Rushed like a torrent o'er her nation,--
192: From their red ruins joy was banished,
193: The gorgeous palace desolate! Maria is the victor's prize;--
198: In recent tomb her father lies; His ancestors repose around, Long freed from life and its alarms; With coronets and princely arms Bedecked their monuments abound!
200: A base successor now holds sway,-- Maria's natal halls his hand
202: And wo throughout the ravaged land.
204: Is fated to the dregs to drain, Immured in Bakchesaria's palace
205: She sighs for liberty in vain;
206: The Khan observes the maiden's pain,
207: His heart is at her grief afflicted,
209: And least of all Maria's will
210: Is by the harem's laws restricted.
211: The hateful guard, of all the dread,
212: Learns silent to respect and fear her, His eye ne'er violates her bed,
214: Nor day nor night he ventures near her;
215: To her he dares not speak rebuke,
216: Nor on her cast suspecting look. Her bath she sought by none attended,
218: Except her chosen female slave, The Khan to her such freedom gave;
223: It seemed as though some jewel rare,
224: Something unearthly were secluded, And careful kept untroubled there.

227: The comfort of the spirit mourning
228: And trust of those to sorrow doomed.

234: And whilst the rest, or sad or gay,
236: The sacred image still concealing, Before it pouring forth her prayer,
237: She watched with ever jealous care;
238: Even as our hearts to error given,
239: Yet lighted by a spark from heaven,
240: Howe'er from virtue's paths we swerve,

248: Scatters the hills and dales along,
249: The lustre of her rays entrancing.
252: The Tartars' wives in garb befitting, They like unprisoned shades were flitting
254: From house to house their friends to see,
255: And while the evening hours away
256: In harmless sports or converse gay.
257: The inmates of the harem slept;--
259: Still was the palace, night impending
260: O'er all her silent empire kept;
261: The eunuch guard, no more offending The fair ones by his presence, now
262: Slumbered, but fear his soul attending
263: Troubled his rest and knit his brow;
265: And on his mind incessant preyed,
266: The air the slightest murmur breaking
267: Assailed his ear with sounds of dread.
268: Now, by some noise deceitful cheated,
269: Starts from his sleep the timid slave,
270: Listens to hear the noise repeated,
271: But all is silent as the grave,
272: Save where the fountains softly sounding
273: Break from their marble prisons free, Or night's sweet birds the scene surrounding
275: Pour forth their notes of melody:
276: Long does he hearken to the strain,
277: Then sinks fatigued in sleep again.
278: Luxurious East! how soft thy nights,
279: What magic through the soul they pour! How fruitful they of fond delights
281: What splendour in each house is found,
285: When angry feelings cease to riot
286: There love inspires with softer sway!
288: The women sleep;--but one is there Who sleeps not; goaded by despair
289: Her couch she quits with dread intent, On awful errand is she bent;
290: Breathless she through the door swift flying
291: Passes unseen; her timid feet Scarce touch the floor, she glides so fleet.
293: The eunuch thwarts the fair one's path,
294: Ah! who can speak his bosom's wrath?
295: False is the quiet sleep would throw Around that gray and care-worn brow;
296: She like a spirit vanished by Viewless, unheard as her own sigh!
298: The door she reaches, trembling opes,
300: Enters, and looks around with awe,
301: What sorrows, anguish, terrors, hopes, Rushed through her heart at what she saw!
303: The image of the sacred maid,
305: And cross attracted first the fair, By the dim lamp-light scarce displayed!
307: The vision burst upon thy soul,
308: The tongue long silent uttered praise,
309: The heart throbs high, but sin's control Cannot escape, 'tis passion, passion sways!
310: The Princess in a maid's repose Slumbered, her cheek, tinged like the rose,
311: By feverish thought, in beauty blooms,
313: And the fresh tear that stains her face
315: Thus cheers the moon fair Flora's race,

319: Vented the feelings of his breast,
320: And for the harem's inmates wept!
322: By anguish urged to mere despair,
323: On bended knee, in tone subdued
324: And melting strain, for pity sued.
325: "Oh! spurn not such a suppliant's prayer!"
326: Her tones so sad, her sighs so deep,
327: Startled the Princess in her sleep;
328: Wond'ring, she views with dread before her The stranger beauty, frighted hears For mercy her soft voice implore her,
330: Raises her up with trembling hand,
331: And makes of her the quick demand,
332: "Who speaks? in night's still hour alone, Wherefore art here?" "A wretched one,
333: To thee I come," the fair replied,
335: Hope, hope alone my soul sustains;
337: And lived from sorrow free and care,
338: But now, alas! a prey to pains And terrors, Princess hear my prayer,
339: Oh! listen, or I am destroyed! Not here beheld I first the light,
340: Far hence my native land, but yet
342: Objects once precious to my sight;
345: Woods pervious scarce to wolf or deer, Nor faith, nor manners such as here;
347: But, by what cruel fate o'ercome,
348: How I was snatched, or when, from home
349: I know not,--well the heaving ocean
350: Do I remember, and its roar,
351: But, ah! my heart such wild commotion
352: As shakes it now ne'er felt before.
353: I in the harem's quiet bloomed,
356: With willing heart what love had doomed;
357: Its secret wishes came to pass:
359: For feats of war no longer burned,
360: Nor, pleased, upon its horrors thought,
361: To these fair scenes again returned.
363: We stood, timid my eyes I raised,
364: When suddenly our glances meeting, I drank in rapture as I gazed;
365: He called me to him,--from that hour
366: We lived in bliss beyond the power
368: Of evil thought or wicked word, The tongue of calumny unheard,
369: Suspicion, doubt, or jealous fear, Of weariness alike unknown, Princess, thou comest a captive here, And all my joys are overthrown, Giray with sinful passion burns, His soul possessed of thee alone, My tears and sighs the traitor spurns; No more his former thoughts, nor feeling For me now cherishes Giray, Scarce his disgust, alas! concealing, He from my presence hastes away. Princess, I know the fault not thine That Giray loves thee, oh! then hear A suppliant wretch, nor spurn her prayer! Throughout the harem none but thou Could rival beauties such as mine Nor make him violate his vow; Yet, Princess! in thy bosom cold The heart to mine left thus forlorn, The love I feel cannot be told, For passion, Princess, was I born.

443: She sleeps; her loss the chieftain grieves, And his neglected harem leaves,

461: Abandoned, pined and sank in age;

494: Upon its vanished greatness pondered; All silent now those spacious halls,
